title: Fallout Tactics: Brotherhood of Steel
text: This game. I have such mixed feelings about this game. I personally enjoyed it a lot but it is definetly not for everyone. On one hand its keyboard smashingly hard at times, the AI is lacking, good luck ever using multiplayer,and the campaign is as linear as the equator. On the other hand its an amazing idea to have a fallout themed turn based strategy with open ended character customization, a good sized aresenal of weapons, and a story that will take a long while to beat allowing you to really flesh out your character to fit your play style.  If you are a die hard fallout fan the yes insta buy this title. Otherwise just keep in mind that this is a hard and long game that can be as fun as you want it to be. It was designed to let you play through levels in a variety of styles. If you choose to be a grenade lobbing madman so be it, if you grind through the game inch by inch at a super slow pace with a squad of nohing but snipers and it didn't seem like any fun its because thats how you decided to play. It doesn't have much replayability but overall I think its a pretty good one and done.

title: Fallout Tactics: Brotherhood of Steel
text: Fallout Tactics can only loosely be considered an actual Fallout game. While using the engine of the first two Fallout games, having the same setting and very similar (yet vastly improved) combat, it lacks the entire story RPG side of things. There are close to no sidequests, there are barely any NPCs, there's no chooseable dialogue whatsoever and companion remain silent and are fully replaceable. But even considering all its shortcomings, Fallout Tactics is basically to Fallout what Icewind Dale is to Baldur's Gate: A great spin-off in the same universe with slightly different focus, yet which deserves just as much attention.

title: Fallout Tactics: Brotherhood of Steel
text: Although "Tactics" is built purely around combat, it's no less challenging than its isometric RPG progenitors. You will probably die a lot, and you will probably reload a lot if losing a squad member permanently is unacceptable to you. Mistakes are punished swiftly (and often brutally), and trying to just blast your way through is rarely a workable approach. As a special note, be sure to save often and incrementally. I nearly made it to the end of the game, but was prevented when a defeated enemy blocked the only route to my goal. Unfortunately, I had made my only save just after the enemy was felled, which would have required me to roll back to the beginning of the area to try again. It had been such an exhausting process to get to that point that I just opted to stop playing. (Having put over 60 hours into the game, I figured that I had seen most of the show anyway.) Anyway - this title is a classic example of game design, and definitely worth checking out. It won't "nursemaid" you, but that's part of what made it the experience that it was.

title: Fallout Tactics: Brotherhood of Steel
text: Fallout Tactics is a very focused squad based version of Fallout. You lose alot of the exploration options of Fallout as well as alot of non combative ways to resolve problems. As consequence it is less about losing yourself in the world as it is about kicking the worlds butt. If you like XCOM there is a very good chance you will enjoy this game. For that matter it is probably closer to Jagged Alliance then XCOM but both are great games. The character leveling system is particularly good and challenges you to balance the diffrent skills so that you have a good medic and a good laser guy for example. Unlike other games of the genre there are melee characters (if you permit) on your squad that allow for some stealth elements of the game. Unlike say XCOM the enemy doesn't neccasirly know you are on the map. I like this alot, it is really cool to move your units around a building, in an attempt to prepare for a perfect assult. It is even cooler to have characters sneaking around disabling mines and slitting the throat of a lonely soldier. Dated graphics but defintely worth the time if you like XCOM or Jagged Alliance.

title: Final Exam
text: Want to beat up a monster with a baseball bat? Or shoot one down with a gun? Or say f_uck it and chop one up with a chainsaw? Well you can do it with Final Exam. You play as one of four best friends visiting their old high school. There they get trapped in an old town infested by monsters, monsters, and more monsters. This is a 2.5D game that uses combos as its main hook. It’s a lot of fun to throw a monster in the air, jump after him, and bash him to the ground. Oh, by the way, there’s monsters. Did I mention that yet? The AI for the enemies is good, but seems fairly easy if you know what you’re doing regarding gameplay and combos. The combat is fluid and visceral as well as exciting. The game’s not all melee combat. You do have a small arsenal of firearms that are a joy to use. In addition to the melee weapons and firearms, there’s also grenades that feel like a bit of a cheat, but are fun to use nonetheless. The locals for the game are well designed and offer a wide variety play styles. One thing you need to know before you buy this game is that it’s centered around co-op. The singleplayer is fine, but multiplayer is where I had most of my fun. Whether locally or online, cooperative play adds a lot to the beat-em-up aspect of the gameplay. Taking on the horde of monsters with a friend is very rewarding. Each player has a tag above their head so you can recognize them among the confusion. Final Exam is a clever action-packed game that is riddled with horror game staples and campy goodness in equal measures. With specialized characters and art to dazzle your eyes, there's something in here for any type of gamer.

text: Disclaimer: I will continue to revise this review as I play more, because I do enjoy the game. Let me preface this by saying that I think the gameplay elements of this game are unmatched by any fishing game that has ever been made. This is without a doubt, as the game says on the loading screen, the best fishing simulator ever. I have no disagreements with that. Fishing planet is immersive, pretty, exciting, and relaxing all in one. The fishing experience is the way it should be in every fishing game. There are a plethora of rods, lines, reels, etc. Some of them make a real difference and others are purely cosmetic. Learning how to catch new fish is a challenge sometimes, as you figure out the right bait, drag setting, line, etc. Everything about it feels like real fishing. However, there are some things which, while true in real life about fishing, don't make for a great experience in a video game. The game is severely gated by the travel fees and staying fees for going places other than the free Lone Star Lake in Texas. It is EXTREMELY hard to cover the cost of the trip while on the trip, LET ALONE turn a profit. So, the way the game plays out for newcomers for a VERY long time is like this... 1) you grind XP and cash on really small boring fish in Lone Star Lake just to save up enough to make a couple day trip somewhere to fish. 2) You go there and catch awesome fish but your net is too small so you can't make a profit or even COVER the charge of the trip. 3) You're now broke and can only fish at Lone Star Lake. 4) Because the catchable fish in Lone Star are for newbies, when that's the only place you can go back to to fish, the amout of time it takes to save up again is EXTREMELY long. As you can see this makes for a very frustrating game experience. Now with a premium accout you can make this process easier, but of course that costs real world money. So in reality, to get the game play experience this game SHOULD have, you have to pay real money and it doesn't seem like a "free game" anymore. I'm going to keep playing this game to see if I'm doing something wrong and find out the methods which make this easier, but as of right now I don't really see how this could play out any different.

title: Fishing Planet
text: I love fishing, I live in FL and fish all the time.  I've been dying for a fishing game that's worth anything since sega dreamcast was around.   I want this title to do well, this game has all the right ideas, all the things I would want in a fishing game.   Since it is early access I won't harp on game mechanics and physics as I know they will improve.  My biggest problem with the game is its just not fun.  Let me explain, in Fl in real life I go to a lake I can catch many species using the same bait by adjusting I how I present it to the fish, where I'm from bass,bluegill,catfish,etc,etc will eat a nightcrawler.  It may not be optimal but it happens.  In this game its not like that at all, I find myself searching guides after frustration sets in.  You then find to catch this species you cast in this exact spot, during this time period, with exact leader setting at this amount, using this exact lure or bait and then grind for hours using that exact setup.  There isn't really any rng.  Once you get the xp needed to reach next lake you then go to guides find exact spot and grind for hours on the next fish.  To me thats not fun. If you don't like grinding you can spend 150$+ of real money to get the better lures, and xp boosts.   I probably don't play this game mostly because of the costly dlc that comes out that you need to buy if you don't want to play for 12 hours a day to compete with others.   The very first day this game came to steam I spent 20$ for a weekly boost of some sort and it does not go by game time it goes by real time so it forces you to play alot to make it feel its worth it purchase.   I would rather this game be 40$ and come with all content then claim to be free to play.   Its free to play to get you in the door then when you feel the grind you pay out the A##.

title: Fishing Planet
text: Update: Early January, 2017. Nothing of importance changed in the past year. The game is still "in development", it still has a relatively tiny group of players, many of whom are hardcore addicts, because this is how the game is ballanced (for addicts). There will be an update soon, many things will change, but, in a sense, everything will stay the same. I'm changing the verdict to Not recommended. Update: Early January, 2016. Early access is over (or it will never end - pick your interpretation). I deleted all of my previous writings. All you need to know is that this is not a hard-core fishing simulator. Not even close. A lot can be improved, but it seems it won't be. I'm saying this based on 30+ years real life angling experience and 1500 fish caught in this game. Also note that you need to be a gamer (i.e. and addict) to progress in it. If' you're a normal human being with life, you will probably be irritated by extremely steep progression. It is to be changed, however, still not clear how. However, it looks pretty and is very addictive. There ARE moments when the illusion is indeed very strong. But they get less frequent and further appart as you play more. Ok, think of it this way.. This game is as ultimate fishing simulator, as latest Call of Duty is the ultimate warfare simulator or Dirt3 - ultimate rally racing simulator. These games may seem that to many, but if you were in the real war or raced real rally cars.... You get the point. Plus, we know that there are much more realistic warfare or rally simulators, so it can be done. With fishing situation is different. This game is quite probably the most realistic at the moment (not counting (very) old ones). But being most realistic doesn't guarantee that one is realistic at all. And judging by all we know at the moment, the game will remain this way. There will be a lot of new content, but the fishing framework will hardly change. Hope I'm wrong.
